subject: Renewal: geo split SLA & EU residency onboarding + APAC staged rollout
messages:
From: Katherine Li <katherine.li@medivance.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: tom.ruiz@medivance.com, priya.menon@medivance.com
Date: 2026-11-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — residency + APAC

Kim,

Thanks for the call earlier. Medivance is generally happy to continue with Redwood, but we need the renewal to reflect two things before procurement will sign: 1) explicit EU data residency guarantees for PHI-scoped traffic, and 2) a staged APAC rollout plan with clear failover behavior (we can accept warm-standby in APAC for months 1–6, then scale to primary region). Also need a separate SLA tranche for EU traffic with a 99.9% target and credits in case of cross-region failover.

Can you send a proposal showing the amended term (18-month commit), the capacity uplift cost for a +2x token baseline in APAC, and the SOW for onboarding/residency validation? Procurement wants something they can hand to legal & security.

Best,
Katherine Li
Director, Cloud Platforms
Medivance Health

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — residency + APAC

Katherine — thanks for the clarity and the list. We've sketched the changes you asked for and attached an initial SOW and SLA proposal. High level: 

- Term: 18-month renewal starting 2027-01-01 with a staged APAC onramp (warm standby months 1–3, capacity seed months 4–6, primary in months 7+).
- EU residency: EU primary node(s) for PHI traffic with customer-managed KMS option; audit log retention window extended to 12 months for the EU tenant.
- SLA split: We can offer a regional SLA carve-out that treats EU-primary traffic under a 99.9% latency & availability baseline and provides credits tied to cross-region failover events (detailed in Redwood-SLA-proposal.pdf).
- Upsell / capacity: baseline token commit uplift +2x for APAC seeding, with a one-time onboarding fee (see SOW_v2_draft.pdf) and estimated ARR delta in the SOW.

Action items we propose:
1) Internal review with your security & legal — we'll incorporate redlines.
2) Technical kickoff (we can schedule a 60-minute session next week) to validate the residency design and test failover triggers.
3) Sign SOW + amendment and then DocuSign for the 18-month commitment.

I copied Ben for pricing confirmation, Marcus for residency ops, and Dylan for rollout sequencing. If that aligns, I'll turn this into a clean amendment and push the DocuSign.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_v2_draft.pdf (20 pages), Redwood-SLA-proposal.pdf (6 pages)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: pricing and capacity notes for Medivance renewal

Team — quick notes after reviewing Kim's draft:

- Pricing: we can provide the 18-month term with the requested regional SLA carve-out. APAC +2x token baseline increases the monthly commit by ~38% (run numbers included in APAC-deployment-matrix.xlsx). Recommend absorbing onboarding fee by offering a 50% discount for the first quarter to keep ARR step reasonable for client.

- Residency: Marcus, can you confirm lead time to provision EU tenant with customer-managed KMS? We should expect a 6–8 week lead for standing up dedicated EU nodes and an additional 2 weeks for integration testing. Include post-cutover validation window (2 weeks).

- Failover: Dylan — we need a clear failover playbook and measurable SLA breach conditions. Suggest automated failover on region degraded metrics + manual failover with on-call approval for partial outages. We should itemize credit calculation (per 10-minute window).

I'll prepare a pricing appendix to attach to the SOW. Kim — want me to include the 50% onboarding discount language and a schedule for the APAC ramp?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
